title: Manifold-Constrained Initial Noise Optimization for Efficient Generative Model Alignment

paper.title: Manifold-Constrained Initial Noise Optimization for Efficient Generative Model Alignment
paper.abstract:
Abstract Recent advances in distillation and flow-map models have enabled deterministic one- or few-step generation for high-quality data, facilitating a new branch of reward alignment approaches that directly optimize the initial noise from a Gaussian distribution. However, most existing initial-noise optimization methods rely on first-order gradient information, which is either inapplicable or suffers from instability and inefficiency in black-box reward scenarios.
Here, we introduce ZeNOVA ( Ze roth-order N oise O ptimization with V alue A nnealing), a stable and efficient initial noise alignment method in a gradient-free manner. Specifically, we address existing algorithms’ major challenge in black-box scenarios through annealed soft-value guidance, manifold-constrained hyperspherical Langevin dynamics, and Metropolis-Hastings jumping.
Extensive experiments on image and video generative models show that ZeNOVA outperforms all evaluated zeroth-order baselines by optimizing the initial noise toward higher rewards substantially more stably while exploiting the geometry of the Gaussian prior, demonstrating its practical applicability to various black-box reward alignment.

sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.text: Reward alignment of a pre-trained generative model aims to align its output distribution to admit higher external reward while minimizing its deviation from the original prior. A wide range of fine-tuning based approaches are presented grounded on several theoretical support, including entropy-regularized reinforcement learning ( Black et al., 2024 ; Fan et al., 2023 ; Liu et al., 2025a ; He et al., 2026 ; Zheng et al., 2026a ) , GFlowNets ( Zhang et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2025c ; Liu et al., 2025b ) , and stochastic optimal control ( Domingo-Enrich et al., 2025 ) . Inference-time methods employing various techniques such as diffusion posterior sampling ( Chung et al., 2023 ; Ye et al., 2024 ; Yu et al., 2023 ; He et al., 2023 ; Song et al., 2023a ) and path integral control ( Huang et al., 2024 ; Kim et al., 2025 ) have also been proposed to implement the same effect without additional training. However, these works have to assume stochastic sampling trajectories involving many intermediate steps for their methods to analytically admit the reward-tilted distribution and thereby satisfy both the prior and high reward. Consequently, naively extending the results of these works to deterministic generative models is either limited or does not guarantee its behavior as theoretically designed. Moreover, recent advances in generative modeling have led to the development of few-step or one-step models including distilled models ( Yin et al., 2024b ; Yin et al., 2024a ; Sauer et al., 2024 ) and flow-map models ( Song et al., 2023b ; Geng et al., 2025 ) , which reduces the effect of control in between intermediate sampling process. Figure 1: Overview of ZeNOVA. Naive initial-noise optimization suffers from limited exploration and unstable updates under inaccurate zeroth-order guidance from raw reward signal. ZeNOVA combines annealed soft-value guidance, hyperspherical updates, and Metropolis-Hastings jumping to enable stable local refinement and global exploration while respecting the Gaussian prior geometry. These recent advances facilitate a separate approach of initial-noise optimization as a practical route to inference-time reward alignment; a pretrained deterministic generator can produce different outputs by changing its Gaussian input, without updating its parameters ( Eyring et al., 2024 ; Min et al., 2026 ; Yoon et al., 2026 ) . Most existing approaches, however, obtain their optimization directions by differentiating through both the generator and the reward computation. This requirement limits their use when the reward is non-differentiable or available only through black-box evaluations, and can impose substantial computational overhead even when gradients are accessible. Estimating directions from reward queries offers a gradient-free alternative, but useful alignment also requires these estimates to support stable and efficient optimization in the high-dimensional noise space. In particular, seeking higher rewards should account for the Gaussian noise input geometry on which the generator was trained, which still remains challenging with optimizations in gradient-free manner. Here, we propose ZeNOVA , a stable and efficient gradient-free initial-noise alignment method toward black-box objectives. Specifically, as illustrated in Figure 1 , we identify the major challenges faced by existing initial noise optimization algorithms in black-box scenarios, and address them through three contributions of annealed soft-value guidance, manifold-constrained hyperspherical Langevin dynamics, and Metropolis-Hastings jumping. Together, these components require only forward evaluations of the generator and reward model, making ZeNOVA applicable to black-box alignment without backpropagation. Experiments on image and video generative models show that ZeNOVA achieves higher rewards than all evaluated zeroth-order baselines while maintaining more stable initial-noise optimization, supporting its practical use across diverse reward alignment tasks.

MH chain targets the same distribution with Langevin dynamics and provides global exploration, but it is inefficient as a stand-alone sampler: Namely, for a finite number of proposals, the MH algorithm is strictly worse than Best-of-K(BoK) sampling. Moreover, as the sample reward increases, every proposal is drawn afresh regardless of the current high-reward state, and the MH algorithm rejects almost all proposals. Nonetheless, this has a complementary behavior against Langevin dynamics, allowing occasional global moves to new reward modes with much smaller computation than gradient estimation. We therefore interleave a small number of independent MH transitions with Langevin updates, dubbed as MH jumping . The two principal hyperparameters governing inference-time computation are the number of particles N N and the number of sampling iteration K K . Increasing N N improves the Monte Carlo estimate of the soft value gradient, while increasing K K allows the sampler to traverse the interpolation more gradually. Importantly, ZeNOVA requires only forward evaluations of the generator and reward model.

We evaluate initial noise alignment for pretrained text-to-image generation with SDXL-turbo ( Sauer et al., 2024 ) and DMD2 ( Yin et al., 2024a ) on five tasks: ImageReward ( Xu et al., 2024 ) , PickScore ( Kirstain et al., 2023 ) , GenEval ( Ghosh et al., 2023 ) , Query object counting ( Qian et al., 2025 ) , and OCR ( Cui et al., 2025 ) . The generator parameters remain fixed, and alignment is performed by updating the initial noise. ImageReward and PickScore provide differentiable preference rewards, while GenEval, Counting, and OCR evaluate compositional alignment, object counting, and text rendering through black-box reward evaluations. We additionally report aesthetic score ( Schuhmann, 2022 ) as a separate evaluation metric to assess how task-specific alignment affects visual quality. See Appendix B.3 for the detailed settings on the reward functions and utilized text prompt datasets. We include uncontrolled generation and Best-of-K, which selects the best sample among K K independently drawn initial noises. The zeroth-order baselines comprise ZO Langevin, exponential-map updates with a ZO gradient estimator, and Natural Evolution Strategies (NES) ( Wierstra et al., 2014 ) . For differentiable rewards, we also include ReNO ( Eyring et al., 2024 ) , ORIGEN ( Min et al., 2026 ) , and MoNO ( Shi et al., 2026 ) as baselines that utilize backpropagation through the generator and reward model. Table 1 shows that ZeNOVA improves over uncontrolled generation, Best-of- K K , and every reported zeroth-order optimization baseline on all five task metrics for both generative models. Specifically, in black-box reward tasks, ZeNOVA achieves performance gains of + 0.046 +0.046 on GenEval and + 0.088 +0.088 on OCR from the best zeroth-order baseline, and reduces MAE of counting by around 40 % 40\% . These results show improvements over the alternatives on objectives that do not provide gradients. Note that on ImageReward and PickScore where the reward gradient is accessible, gradient-based algorithms of ReNO and ORIGEN often attain higher reward than ours. Here, leveraging the fact that ImageReward and PickScore both measure the same aspect of human preference, we evaluated both runs with the reward not employed during optimization as a validation metric. We observe that gradient-based methods are prone to reward hacking, allowing our method to achieve the highest validation metric. In terms of image quality, ZeNOVA achieved the highest Aesthetic score across various scenarios, while some unstable zeroth-order methods and first-order methods prone to reward hacking exhibited significant drops. While this is partly because some optimized rewards are already associated with image quality, but the results in other cases suggest that ZeNOVA properly preserves the prior distribution of the original generative model’s input. sections.heading: 5 Discussion
sections.text: Effect of Particle Count per Iteration. Zeroth-order methods require reward evaluations for a fixed number( N N ) of particles per iteration to estimate each method’s intended update direction of the initial noise; as N N increases, this estimate approaches the theoretical ground truth and the performance converges. In practice, since the number of available reward evaluations is finite, the performance behavior with a small number of particles becomes a critical factor in the practicality of the algorithm. Figure 6: Effect of particle count per iteration for zeroth-order methods. Figure 7: Pareto curve between PickScore and Vendi diversity at different guidance scales. Figure 6 compares ZeNOVA with Cartesian Langevin, exponential-map updates, and NES with ImageReward on HPDv2 prompts, holding the number of iterations fixed at K = 25 K=25 . Reward increases with N N for every evaluated method, while ZeNOVA achieves the highest reward at every reported particle count and exhibits a small degradation as the particle budget decreases; reducing N N from 64 64 to 8 8 lowers ZeNOVA’s ImageReward by only 0.0743 0.0743 . Notably, ZeNOVA with only 8 8 particles outperforms all three baselines with 64 64 particles. These results demonstrate that ZeNOVA preserves strong alignment under limited reward-query budgets and are consistent with the stabilizing role of hyperspherical updates under noisy zeroth-order guidance. Reward-Diversity Trade-off. ZeNOVA and the baselines have a guidance scale hyperparameter λ \lambda to control the trade-off between prior preservation and reward. Figure 7 plots the Pareto curve between PickScore reward and Vendi diversity ( Friedman and Dieng, 2023 ) of 64 images per prompt, for different methods at three guidance scales. For all methods, increasing 1 / λ 1/\lambda improves the average reward while diversity decreases, indicating that stronger guidance yields reward gains by making the output distribution focus on a narrow high-reward region. Meanwhile, our approach achieves a dominant Pareto front located at the most upright of the plot, indicating higher diversity in its output for a fixed level of reward alignment. We’ve conducted an ablation study on more detailed design choices of the proposed ZeNOVA in Table 3 to analyze and emphasize their role. It is shown that all three components contributed to the method’s performance and stability. We note that introducing the annealed soft value function yielded marginal or no performance improvements on ImageReward and PickScore, but led to a substantial improvement on OCR reward; the reward landscapes of the former two rewards are continuous with many high-reward modes, allowing sufficiently high rewards to be achieved using only local reward gradient information around the initial point. In the more challenging black-box reward of OCR, the value function allows the method to access a more global and meaningful reward gradient signal.

sections.heading: 6 Conclusion
sections.text: We introduced ZeNOVA, a stable and efficient initial-noise optimization framework for generative models through initial-noise optimization. Guided by a reward-tilted sampling objective, ZeNOVA combines annealed soft-value guidance to extract useful signals from irregular rewards, where several crucial challenges are adequately resolved to enable stability and global exploration. Experimental results on various scenarios demonstrate that ZeNOVA consistently achieves higher rewards than the zeroth-order baselines and retains strong performance with less computational cost.

B.3 Text-to-Image Generation
sections.text: Models. We utilized SDXL-turbo ( Sauer et al., 2024 ) and DMD2 ( Yin et al., 2024a ) without Classifier-Free Guidance scale for our text-to-image generative models. All experiments for zeroth-order methods are conducted using NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPUs with VRAM 24GB. For first-order methods which require backpropagation through reward model and generator, NVIDIA A100 with VRAM 40GB was used. Reward function and text prompts. ImageReward ( Xu et al., 2024 ) and PickScore ( Kirstain et al., 2023 ) return the human preference of a given image related to the text prompt. GenEval ( Ghosh et al., 2023 ) evaluates the alignment between a given image and text prompt by aggregating detection result for text attributes. For counting reward, we employ an external model T2ICount ( Qian et al., 2025 ) that estimates the count of given query objects in a given image. Here, to implement a challenging black-box reward scenario, we rounded the continuous T2ICount output to a nearest whole number before used by any initial noise optimization methods. OCR reward is computed using PaddleOCR ( Cui et al., 2025 ) according to a normalized Levenshtein distance between the recognized and target text. For counting reward task, we imported a quantity-aware generation prompt set from Yoon et al. (2026) which contains text prompts of various objects attached with a certain query number. For other tasks, we used HPDv2 ( Wu et al., 2023 ) prompts for ImageReward, Pick-a-Pic ( Kirstain et al., 2023 ) prompts for PickScore and OCR, GenEval test prompts for GenEval, where we randomly selected 200 prompts. Hyperparameters. For the results in Table 1 , we use N = 16 N=16 particles per update for the particle-based zeroth-order optimization methods. The number of iteration was set to K = 25 K=25 for ImageReward and Counting, and K = 50 K=50 for PickScore, GenEval, and OCR. These settings correspond to N × K = 400 N\times K=400 and 800 800 number of reward function evaluations, respectively. First-order methods require one function evaluation and its backpropagation per iteration, so we allocated N × K N\times K iterations for each task. Note that ZeNOVA utilized N MH N_{\text{MH}} number of reward evaluations for MH jumping, so only N − N MH N-N_{\text{MH}} number of particles were used for value gradient estimation unlike other zeroth-order methods. We used N MH = 4 N_{\text{MH}}=4 for all tasks. We set the guidance scale to 1 / λ = 100.0 1/\lambda=100.0 for the Counting reward and 1 / λ = 1000.0 1/\lambda=1000.0 for the rest of the reward function, unless specified. Step size for ZeNOVA was set to η A = 0.1 \eta_{A}=0.1 and η R = 0.03 \eta_{R}=0.03 . Affiliation: Kim Jaechul Graduate School of AI Affiliation: KAIST Affiliation: Seoul, South Korea Email: {jinhojsk515,jong.ye}@kaist.ac.kr Abstract Recent advances in distillation and flow-map models have enabled deterministic one- or few-step generation for high-quality data, facilitating a new branch of reward alignment approaches that directly optimize the initial noise from a Gaussian distribution. However, most existing initial-noise optimization methods rely on first-order gradient information, which is either inapplicable or suffers from instability and inefficiency in black-box reward scenarios. Here, we introduce ZeNOVA ( Ze roth-order N oise O ptimization with V alue A nnealing), a stable and efficient initial noise alignment method in a gradient-free manner. Specifically, we address existing algorithms’ major challenge in black-box scenarios through annealed soft-value guidance, manifold-constrained hyperspherical Langevin dynamics, and Metropolis-Hastings jumping. Extensive experiments on image and video generative models show that ZeNOVA outperforms all evaluated zeroth-order baselines by optimizing the initial noise toward higher rewards substantially more stably while exploiting the geometry of the Gaussian prior, demonstrating its practical applicability to various black-box reward alignment. 1 Introduction Reward alignment of a pre-trained generative model aims to align its output distribution to admit higher external reward while minimizing its deviation from the original prior. A wide range of fine-tuning based approaches are presented grounded on several theoretical support, including entropy-regularized reinforcement learning ( Black et al., 2024 ; Fan et al., 2023 ; Liu et al., 2025a ; He et al., 2026 ; Zheng et al., 2026a ) , GFlowNets ( Zhang et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2025c ; Liu et al., 2025b ) , and stochastic optimal control ( Domingo-Enrich et al., 2025 ) . Inference-time methods employing various techniques such as diffusion posterior sampling ( Chung et al., 2023 ; Ye et al., 2024 ; Yu et al., 2023 ; He et al., 2023 ; Song et al., 2023a ) and path integral control ( Huang et al., 2024 ; Kim et al., 2025 ) have also been proposed to implement the same effect without additional training. However, these works have to assume stochastic sampling trajectories involving many intermediate steps for their methods to analytically admit the reward-tilted distribution and thereby satisfy both the prior and high reward. Consequently, naively extending the results of these works to deterministic generative models is either limited or does not guarantee its behavior as theoretically designed. Moreover, recent advances in generative modeling have led to the development of few-step or one-step models including distilled models ( Yin et al., 2024b ; Yin et al., 2024a ; Sauer et al., 2024 ) and flow-map models ( Song et al., 2023b ; Geng et al., 2025 ) , which reduces the effect of control in between intermediate sampling process. Figure 1: Overview of ZeNOVA. Naive initial-noise optimization suffers from limited exploration and unstable updates under inaccurate zeroth-order guidance from raw reward signal. ZeNOVA combines annealed soft-value guidance, hyperspherical updates, and Metropolis-Hastings jumping to enable stable local refinement and global exploration while respecting the Gaussian prior geometry. These recent advances facilitate a separate approach of initial-noise optimization as a practical route to inference-time reward alignment; a pretrained deterministic generator can produce different outputs by changing its Gaussian input, without updating its parameters ( Eyring et al., 2024 ; Min et al., 2026 ; Yoon et al., 2026 ) . Most existing approaches, however, obtain their optimization directions by differentiating through both the generator and the reward computation. This requirement limits their use when the reward is non-differentiable or available only through black-box evaluations, and can impose substantial computational overhead even when gradients are accessible. Estimating directions from reward queries offers a gradient-free alternative, but useful alignment also requires these estimates to support stable and efficient optimization in the high-dimensional noise space. In particular, seeking higher rewards should account for the Gaussian noise input geometry on which the generator was trained, which still remains challenging with optimizations in gradient-free manner. Here, we propose ZeNOVA , a stable and efficient gradient-free initial-noise alignment method toward black-box objectives. Specifically, as illustrated in Figure 1 , we identify the major challenges faced by existing initial noise optimization algorithms in black-box scenarios, and address them through three contributions of annealed soft-value guidance, manifold-constrained hyperspherical Langevin dynamics, and Metropolis-Hastings jumping. Together, these components require only forward evaluations of the generator and reward model, making ZeNOVA applicable to black-box alignment without backpropagation. Zeroth-order methods require reward evaluations for a fixed number( N N ) of particles per iteration to estimate each method’s intended update direction of the initial noise; as N N increases, this estimate approaches the theoretical ground truth and the performance converges. Guided by a reward-tilted sampling objective, ZeNOVA combines annealed soft-value guidance to extract useful signals from irregular rewards, where several crucial challenges are adequately resolved to enable stability and global exploration. Experimental results on various scenarios demonstrate that ZeNOVA consistently achieves higher rewards than the zeroth-order baselines and retains strong performance with less computational cost.
